Left illustration captioned in image: "It is perfectly ridiculous – the way I hate to demerit the girls"; signed "OKeeffe." Right illustration captioned in image: Whoooeee but – this goes pretty well"; signed "O'Keeffe." 
(Source: Lynes, 1999)

remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. Published in Chatham Episcopal Institute yearbook, *Mortar Board*, 1905, of which O'Keeffe was art editor. Copy consulted owned by Chatham Hall (formerly Chatham Episcopal Institute), Chatham, Virginia. Reproductions of signed illustrations; whereabouts of originals unknown. Published on page 42. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Reproduction of signed illustration. A woman with curly hair and glasses, seen in profile, cries and looks downward. Text overlapping the image reads, "It is perfectly ridiculous  ‚Äî the way I hate to demerit the girls."  To the right of this illustration, another woman, seen from the side, sits at a piano with upright posture. The woman wears a dress and glasses, her curly hair pinned in a bun. Text overlaps the image. Both drawings bear O'Keeffe's signature.
dimensions: 6 1/8 x 8 or 8 x 6 1/8 inches, sheet orientations vary
